analysis.title: Market Update US, Europe & Asia (12 November 2026)
key_insights: US equities closed higher Wednesday: S&P +1.31%, Nasdaq +1.60%, Dow +0.49%. The AI trade led, with neoclouds the standouts. SOX posted its third strong gain in four sessions and is up about 17% from last Thursday's sharp drop. The equal-weight S&P trailed the cap-weighted index by about 50 bp.

The rally followed well-received CoreWeave earnings, positive headlines on Anthropic's coming IPO, a strong acceleration in OpenAI's Q3 revenue growth and continued positioning support. NVDA stabilized while MSFT, AMZN and META were weaker.
The dollar index rose 0.7%, gold fell 0.7%, silver gained 1.5% and WTI settled up 0.6%, off best levels.

The US bond market was closed for Veterans Day after a big backup in Treasury yields on Tuesday that followed a hotter-than-expected CPI print and hawkish Fed comments. Thursday brings jobless claims, a $25B 30-year bond auction and several Fed speakers.
Friday's October PPI has taken outsized importance: headline expected +0.4% m/m after +1.3% in September, core expected +0.3% after +0.7%.

Treasury yields recorded their steepest daily rise since April 2025 on Tuesday. Waller mentioned the possibility of a 50 bp move, Logan said quicker hikes may be needed, Goolsbee called the CPI report disturbing and Bowman said there is still work to do. Markets price about an 85% chance of a December Fed hike and a greater likelihood of three more in 2027, versus two before the CPI data.

CoreWeave (+24.7%) beat and raised with a $132.5B backlog. Management said growth can be financed via customer prepayments (about $9B in the next three months), asset-level debt, vendor financing and cash flow. It will not issue parent-level unsecured debt through 2027 and sees parent-level capital needs below $5B through 2027. About 300K GPUs roll off in 2027-28, with renewals potentially generating nearly $10B with no added capex.

Anthropic's bankers are reportedly targeting a $1.5T IPO valuation, up from an initial $1.4T target, with orders multiple times the shares available (FT, Bloomberg). A higher price would lift the raise to over $100B. OpenAI reported $10B quarterly revenue for the period ending September, up 50% from the prior quarter, with ARR of $50B, while seeking funding at a $1.25T valuation versus the $1.5T investors first sought (Reuters).

The Trump administration is adopting an economic-pressure strategy on Iran, including a naval blockade operation called Iron Gate. Rubio said major combat operations are no longer needed and a diplomatic deal is unlikely soon. Iran says it would reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US meets seven preconditions. Al Arabiya reported a preliminary deal allowing down-blending of enriched uranium to 3.67%, IAEA inspections and release of $6-9B of frozen assets.

Costco announced a $30/share special dividend and $4B buyback. Other US movers: Riskified +22.3%, Rumble +16.6%, Firefly Aerospace +12.3%, Mercury Systems +5.7% on a beat and raise. Decliners: Applied Aerospace & Defense -13.3% on a FY guidance cut, Suja Life -12.9% (Goldman downgrade to neutral), Grocery Outlet -6.4% on lower EBITDA guidance.

European equities closed higher with cyclicals leading. Germany +1.2%, UK +0.8%, France +0.7%. The OAT-Bund spread narrowed about 1.3bp to 146.8bp. Technology led on renewed AI infrastructure enthusiasm, boosting European chip stocks.

ECB chief economist Lane backs a December hike if data does not shift and expects inflation slightly above 4% by year-end, with food and core prices accelerating in early 2027. October eurozone PMI eased to a four-month low of 51.7, but S&P Global says growth is trending at about 0.3% a quarter.

Bundesbank's Nagel signaled an upward revision to German growth forecasts next month. The government upgraded its 2026 forecast to 1.3%, with 2027 growth forecast at a relatively weak 1%. Potential growth of 0.3%-0.4% was called too weak.

NIESR says the BoE may need to hike to 5% next year and expects inflation to peak at 4.4% in February. Markets price Bank Rate reaching 4.75% next year. Sell-side economists expect another BoE hike in February, though deputy governor Lombardelli said December is live.

Dutch TTF gas rose for a second session after falling from an early-November peak near €104/MWh to about €79/MWh on Monday. Europe's energy import bill is up over €127B since the Iran conflict began. Sell-side analysts forecast a winter average between €70 and €90/MWh.

Merz is linking an EU budget deal to Ukraine financing and threatened to veto the 2028-2034 budget. The EU has promised to cover two-thirds of Ukraine's €70B gap (about €45B), most likely through joint debt. A special summit is set for the end of the month.

European movers: Siemens Energy +10.7% (Q4 EPS beat, buyback expanded to up to €9B through FY30), FLSmidth +5.6%, RWE +2.2%. Decliners: CSG -20.3% (Q3 revenue miss, FY margin guidance cut), Voestalpine -5.9%, Alcon -4.4% (narrowed FY guidance below consensus), Taylor Wimpey -4.3%, Vestas -3.8%.

Asian equities were mixed: Japan +1.31%, Hong Kong -1.06% (Hang Seng at the bottom of its trading range), China -0.46%. India was notably higher, led by banks. JGB and regional sovereign yields jumped from recent lows.

The BOJ is weighing a third hike in a year, the first time since 1989. OIS pricing for a December hike fell to 52% last Friday from 79% after the Nikkei's third-largest absolute drop on record, and has since recovered to 76% on Tuesday. The October Summary of Opinions was mostly hawkish.

China is discussing a possible 25% tax on interest income from government bonds. One estimate says it could imply a 52 bp rise in the 10Y CGB yield to keep the same after-tax return. The China 10Y yield trades near a record low, and banks are raising dollar deposit rates to curb yuan strength, with the currency near its highest since May 2022.

SoftBank reported a Q2 net loss of JPY1.115T ($7.1B), its biggest since 3Q24, with an H1 impairment of about JPY600B tied to US AI data center procurement costs. NAV fell JPY12.5T to JPY59.9T in September versus June and LTV rose 2.9 ppt to 15.9%. TSMC is to invest $500M each into Anthropic and OpenAI. Alibaba's T-Head filed for a Hong Kong IPO.
Honda (-4.5%) booked a further $3B in EV-related costs but raised its full-year outlook. Korean game stocks Shift Up (-14.5%) and Krafton (-9.6%) fell on Q3 operating profit misses.

market_movers.rationale: Q3 beat and raise with a $132.5B backlog, no parent-level unsecured debt through 2027, and pricing on new contracts rising materially. Stock +24.7%.

earnings_insights: CoreWeave Q3 reported: beat and guided above, backlog $132.5B, stock +24.7%.
Riskified Q3 reported: earnings and revenue beat, FY guidance raised, stock +22.3%.
Rumble Q3 reported: adjusted EBITDA and revenue beat, Q4 revenue guide brackets consensus, stock +16.6%.
Mercury Systems FQ1 reported: EPS, revenue and EBITDA sharply beat, EBITDA margin up about 650bps y/y, FY27 outlook raised, stock +5.7%.
Applied Aerospace & Defense Q3 reported: earnings and revenue better, FY guidance ranges cut, stock -13.3%.
Grocery Outlet Q3 reported: EPS in line, revenue beat, EBITDA missed, comps +0.5%, FY26 comp outlook raised but EBITDA guidance lowered, stock -6.4%.
Siemens Energy Q4 reported EPS €1.49 vs estimate €1.39. FY27 guidance: comparable revenue growth 14-16% and profit margin before special items 14-16% vs margin estimate of 14.2%. Stock +10.7%.

Alcon Q3 reported core EPS $0.91 vs consensus $0.88, revenue $2.72B vs consensus $2.73B. FY core EPS growth guidance narrowed to 12-14% (consensus 13.8%) and revenue growth to about 6% (consensus 7.1%). Stock -4.4%.
CSG Q3 reported revenue €1.51B vs estimate €1.81B. FY operating EBIT margin guidance cut to about 21% from 24-25%. Stock -20.3%.
Voestalpine Q2 reported EPS €0.55 vs consensus €0.57, revenue €3.66B vs €3.81B. FY EBITDA guidance upper end lowered to €1.70B from €1.85B. Stock -5.9%.
Vestas Q3 reported net income €323M vs consensus €380M, revenue €5.68B vs €6.00B. Stock -3.8%.
ABN AMRO Q3 reported net income €939M vs consensus €782M. Stock -1%.
RWE 9M reported adjusted EBITDA €4.58B vs consensus €4.43B, 2026 earnings expected towards the upper end of the €5.75-6.35B range. Stock +2.2%.
SoftBank Q2 reported net loss JPY1.115T ($7.1B), driven by AI-related impairments. Stock -0.4%.
